# `pyrite` CLI reference

Version: `0.34.0`

<!-- Generated by pyrite-dev cli-reference --write; do not edit by hand. -->

Current command reference generated from live Click definitions. See
[README](https://github.com/Quantum-Light-Matter-Cooperative-QLMC/pyrite#readme) for scientific workflow,
[cluster guide](../../guides/running-on-a-cluster.md) for scheduler templates,
[repository map](../../repo_map.md) for implementation ownership, and
[deprecations](cli-deprecations.md) for retired-spelling replacements and
removal versions. Regenerate this page with `pyrite-dev cli-reference --write`.

Remote lab defaults: `--chunk-minutes 10` runs one material at a time in
self-resubmitting slices. `--chunk-minutes 0` selects one monolithic
`UNLIMITED` allocation; that mode defaults to one material process and
accepts at most four. Context-backed values use one precedence chain:
per-call flag, then `PYRITE_*`, then the config store, then the built-in
default. `PYRITE_PROFILE` and `PYRITE_REMOTE_HOST` are the environment tiers.
`pyrite run PROFILE --remote` runs the profile membership; `-m MATERIAL`
narrows it to one material. Compute-performance measurement is isolated
behind `pyrite-dev perf PROFILE`; it accepts the same selectors.

Checkpoint operations use the grouped `pyrite checkpoint ...` paths. The
top-level `slim`, `rebrem`, `reline`, `archive`, `restore`, `archives`,
and `union` spellings were removed at 0.3.0 and now exit as unknown
commands.

Validation uses `pyrite app validation` and `pyrite material validate`; the
Zhai reproduction uses `pyrite app validation reproduce`, which runs locally unless
`--remote` is given. Remote runs use
`pyrite run --remote`. The `check`, `check-config`, `remote run`,
`remote validate`, and `remote check` spellings were removed at 0.3.0.
Energy-grid job lifecycle uses `pyrite remote job ...`; the
former `pyrite energy-grid` job paths were removed at the same time.
User grid derivation and inspection live below `pyrite numerics energy-grid`;
normal runs size line grids automatically and resolve continuum bounds per case.
Explicit derivation requires `--material` and `--energy`
until 0.15.0; optional derivation requires explicit material/energy selection then.
Artifact mutation and verification use `pyrite-dev energy-grid`.

`pyrite profile` writes your profiles to the user catalog layer
(`catalog.user`, the platform config directory by default) and treats the
bundled demo profiles as read-only; `pyrite-dev profile` is the same tree
for maintainers editing the shipped demos.

Automation contract: usage errors exit 2; runtime failures exit 1;
interrupted viewers exit 130; resumable compute exits 75. Diagnostics,
warnings, prompts, and progress use stderr. `-o/--output json` emits one UTF-8
object plus newline with `schema`, `schema_version`, `ok`, `payload`,
and `errors` fields and no human prose on stdout. `table` is the human
default; `wide` is human-only and not a stable automation contract.

Destructive commands preview exact targets by default. In a TTY, accept the
`[y/N]` prompt to execute; in non-interactive use, pass `-y/--yes`.
`pyrite remote job stop` requires JOBID or an explicit selector.

## Command families

Choose a family for its complete help, options, defaults, and examples.

- [`pyrite run`](cli-reference-run.md) — Run a catalog profile's MC sweeps or one ephemeral pixel scene.
- [`pyrite app`](cli-reference-app.md) — Launch or export interactive analysis notebooks.
- [`pyrite checkpoint`](cli-reference-checkpoint.md) — Inspect and manipulate local simulation checkpoints.
- [`pyrite trajectories`](cli-reference-trajectories.md) — List, describe, export, and score saved trajectory captures.
- [`pyrite config`](cli-reference-config.md) — Set and inspect environment-scoped CLI defaults.
- [`pyrite remote`](cli-reference-remote.md) — [dev] Push code and run or manage MC sweeps on a remote GPU box over SSH.
- [`pyrite profile`](cli-reference-profile.md) — Manage catalog scan profiles (named campaign defaults).
- [`pyrite physics`](cli-reference-physics.md) — Manage named physics presets: models, cutoffs, straggling and emission.
- [`pyrite numerics`](cli-reference-numerics.md) — Manage named numerics presets: sampling, reflections/mosaic, integration.
- [`pyrite material`](cli-reference-material.md) — Add, inspect, validate, and blaze individual materials.
- [`pyrite beam`](cli-reference-beam.md) — Manage named beams (``[beams.*]``), attachable to profiles by name.
- [`pyrite detector`](cli-reference-detector.md) — Manage named detector geometries, attachable to profiles by name.
- [`pyrite filter`](cli-reference-filter.md) — Manage reusable downstream filter presets, separate from placements.
- [`pyrite target`](cli-reference-target.md) — Manage reusable slab and stack targets, attached per profile material.
- [`pyrite tables`](cli-reference-tables.md) — Inspect generated cross-section tables and external code trees.
- [`pyrite cache`](cli-reference-cache.md) — Inspect, warm, and clear compiled CPU (Numba) and GPU (CuPy) kernel caches.

## Command tree

## `pyrite`

```text
Usage: pyrite [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Manage coherent X-ray radiation simulation campaigns.

  Start with a named profile: it defines campaign ranges, workloads, and material
  membership. Then run campaigns, inspect checkpoints, or open analysis notebooks.

  Run ``pyrite COMMAND --help`` for command options, units, defaults, and side effects.

  Examples:
    pyrite config setup
    pyrite profile list
    pyrite profile show sub_100keV
    pyrite run sub_100keV -m hopg
    pyrite run sub_100keV --remote --dry-run
    pyrite app analysis launch

Options:
  --version                    Show the version and exit.
  --color [auto|always|never]  Color human output: auto for terminals, always, or never.
                               [default: auto]
  --catalog PATH               Use a complete catalog file or directory for this
                               command; overrides PYRITE_CATALOG and catalog.path. Edits
                               write there.
  -h, --help                   Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  run           Run a profile's MC sweeps and write checkpoints.
  app           Launch or export interactive analysis notebooks.
  checkpoint    Inspect and manipulate local simulation checkpoints.
  trajectories  List, describe, export, and score saved trajectory captures.
  config        Set profile, catalog, workspace, and remote defaults.
  remote        Run and manage MC sweeps on a remote GPU host.
  profile       Manage named catalog campaigns and material membership.
  physics       Manage named physics presets: models, cutoffs and emission.
  numerics      Manage named numerics presets: sampling, mosaic and integration.
  material      Inspect, validate, edit, and blaze individual materials.
  beam          Manage named beams, attachable to profiles by name.
  detector      Manage named detector geometries.
  filter        Manage named reusable downstream filter plates and sequences.
  target        Manage named reusable slab and stack targets.
  tables        Inspect generated cross-section tables and external code trees.
  cache         Inspect and clear compiled CPU/GPU kernel caches.
```
